note.question: How does concealment shape assortment rotation and the value?
note.overview: Assortment rotation—the retailing practice of changing the assortment of products offered to customers—has recently been used as a competitive advantage for both brick-and-mortar and online retailers. We focus on product categories where consumers may purchase multiple products during a season and investigate a new reason why frequent assortment rotations can be valuable to a retailer. Namely, by distributing its seasonal catalog of products over multiple assortments rotated throughout the season, as opposed to selling all products in a single, fixed assortment, the retailer effectively conceals a portion of its full product catalog from consumers, injecting uncertainty into the consumer’s relative product valuations.

During a given selling season, we suppose that a retailer (it) has a potential catalog of N unique products, within a certain product category, for sale to a market of homogeneous consumers, whose size is normalized to 1 without loss of generality.

Before the season begins, the retailer may choose either (i) a fixed assortment strategy, where the assortment is unchanged throughout the entire selling season, or (ii) a sequential assortment strategy where it offers each product sequentially over the course of the selling season.
